title: The Second Opinion (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word cabaret 104bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan male vocal absurdist observational comedy warm
lyrics:
[Intro - piano bar, measured delivery]
I want to tell you about a man
Who went to see his doctor on a Thursday
The doctor looked at him for a while
And said he was absolutely fine

[Verse 1]
But the man was not entirely convinced
He'd read some things, he'd done some sums
He thought it prudent, in the circumstances
To seek a second opinion from someone

He found another doctor on the other side of town
Sat in the waiting room for forty minutes
Looked at a magazine from 2009
And thought about whether he'd made the right decision

[Pre-Chorus]
The second doctor listened carefully
Reviewed the notes from doctor number one
Looked up slowly from his reading glasses
And said what I'm about to say may surprise you son

[Chorus]
In my professional opinion
And I've been doing this for thirty years
In my professional opinion
Your first doctor was right
You don't need a second opinion
You needed your first doctor to say it twice
Second opinion, same conclusion
He was right the first time

[Verse 2]
The man drove home in moderate traffic
Considered the forty-minute wait
The magazine from 2009 had a recipe in it
He thought he might make the pasta on the following Saturday

[Bridge - spoken, completely level]
He did not make the pasta
He was absolutely fine
The first doctor sent a card at Christmas
The second doctor did not
He feels there may be a lesson in that
He's not sure what it is

[Chorus]
In my professional opinion
And I've been doing this for thirty years
In my professional opinion
Your first doctor was right
You don't need a second opinion
You needed your first doctor to say it twice
Second opinion, same conclusion
He was right the first time

[Outro - piano resolves quietly]
He is, to this day, absolutely fine
He had the pasta the following Tuesday
It was reasonable
He did not seek a third opinion on the pasta
